chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Aziz ibn Yahya al-Basri al-Jaloudi in Basra narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdillah Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Jawhari informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umara narrated to us, from his father, from Jabir ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both)

He said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah al-Ansari say: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) passed by an epileptic man while people were gathered around him looking at him, and he said (peace be upon him and his Family): 'For what have these people gathered?' It was said to him: 'For an insane man who is undergoing epilepsy.' Then he looked at him and said: 'He is not insane. Shall I not inform you of the truly insane man?' They said: 'Yes, O Messenger of Allah.' He said: 'Indeed, the truly insane man is the one who swaggers in his walk, looks at the height of the road, and moves his sides with his shoulders. That is the insane one, and this (man) is afflicted.'

key_terms.الْمُبْتَلَى: The afflicted (one with a specific trial/illness)
key_terms.الْمُتَبَخْتِرَ: The one who swaggers / walks with pride
key_terms.حَقَّ الْمَجْنُونِ: The truly insane / The real insane
key_terms.عَطْفِهِ: The height of the road / where one turns or looks

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between an epileptic and the truly insane according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies the distinction between physical epilepsy (as seen in the man struck down) and spiritual madness, defining the latter as arrogance manifested in one's gait and demeanor. This interpretation aligns with Shia exegetical tradition, which often links 'insanity' in a moral sense to the loss of *haya* (modesty) and self-awareness before God. The Prophet’s observation serves as a practical guide for distinguishing between medical affliction and character flaws rooted in pride.
